Does anyone here have a pet pig? How hard are they to care for? What makes a pig a good pet?

They can be housebroken, so thats a plus.

Also, free porkchops.
"Free" in the sense that you have to feed them for years and provide litter and clean up after them and walk them.

I don't own one but have always wanted one so I've done some research, and from what I've gathered they actually make decent pets. They can be house trained (some micro pig breeders will even have then litter box trained when you pick them up), you can do things like teach them to sit and what not. They're hypoallergenic. That being said they will manipulate you to get food, they can become easily stressed and need a lot of attention and can become pretty destructive without it (they get bored like any other pet). So I personally wouldn't recommend them as a pet if you don't have the time to give them the attention they need (as I would with any pet really).

A friend got a miniature Vietnamese potbellied pig as a pet. It was super cute as a baby, but squealed if you tried to pick it up.

Then it started growing. Within a couple of years it wasn't at all miniature: it had grown to about 200lbs. It was only kinda friendly and preferred to be left alone.

So not only was it not a great pet, it also was a lot of work to deal with. Moral of the story: before you buy a miniature pig, make sure it's really miniature.

I make a lot of different beers myself, so I just invite them over, give them some free samples and open them up to a new world.

Since I live in Texas I usually give them a Shiner Bock. If they like that then I give them a Sierra Nevada, usually one of each to test their variety. If they like IPAs, then I'll hand them a Sculpin or Grapefruit Sculpin. If they like stouts the I'll give them a Founder's Breakfast Stout. If they like the more mellow and light beers, I suggest a Heffewiezen.
Shiner or Revolver is a good go-to

So far I haven't had anyone say they hate Bell's Two Hearted. Left Hand's Nitro Milk Stout is another one I've found a lot of people enjoy right off the bat. Sometimes just a good lager, like Great Lakes' Dortmunder Gold is what turns a lifetime macro lager drinker on to the idea of beer with flavor.

Also, a local staple that almost everyone enjoys and even a good chunk of the macro drinkers have already had is Rohrbach's Scotch Ale. It's a very nice example of the style, and it's intimidating and mild enough that most people get into it right off the bat... and it's also how a lot of new craft drinkers quickly learn that they can't drink a smooth 7% beer that goes down very easy the same way they do their Bud/Blue Light.

If we are talking about unique stories I found Kala's to be the most interesting. On a very surface level it is about her deciding to marry the guy. However, once you go beyond the surface level it is a story about India broadly. The country is divided socially between traditions and Westernization. The choices she makes are all about her determining for herself where she falls into those two options. She is a deeply religious person who is also a scientist. Her story is about the simply but essential competing narratives that everyone faces. I found Kala's story to be the most interesting because it lacked any clear morality.

I really liked the show personally. It felt like something different. Which is refreshing.

I thought the characters were fairly real and relatable considering they come from all walks of life. Plus there are some really great choreographed fight scenes that are exciting and fun to watch. The show feels like it has a little something for everyone which is impressive considering that science fiction isn't really everyone's cup of tea.

There is some beautiful camera work in the show as well as some very pretty establishing shots. Overall I was very impressed with the whole show. I love the world that the creators and staff have built for us because it's grounded and yet so fantastic. Wouldn't it be amazing to find out that you are one of these people and you can channel the some other persons mental/physical skills on the fly?
